newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom edges back after 1st half result.
newsitem.headline: Telecom edges back after 1st half result.

text.p: Telecom Corp of New Zealand Ltd edged off its earlier record high to trade at NZ$7.52, down 10 cents, after news of its first half result and a planned NZ$1.0 billion share buyback.
Telecom, which earlier hit a record high of NZ$7.75, announced an increase in net profit to NZ$360.9 million in the six months to September against $338.0 million the same period a year earlier.
Nigel Scott at BZW said his first impressions were that the size of the buyback was lower than some had expected and the result itself was at the lower end of expectations.
Market forecasts were for a net profit of NZ$360-375 million.
Scott said it was difficult to form an opinion on the buyback because the price at which it will be pitched was still unknown.
"I think there were a few players out there who were thinking it might have been a slightly larger buyback, so the market may have just run ahead a little bit of itself," Scott said.
